title: Non-Abelian BRST Cohomology and Classical BV Data

items.title: Finite-Jet Non-Abelian BRST Complex
items.statement:
Let $n\geq 1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty open set with coordinates $x^1,\ldots,x^n$, and let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra with bilinear alternating bracket $[\ ,\ ]_{\mathfrak g}$ satisfying the Jacobi identity. Let $V=V_{\bar 0}\oplus V_{\bar 1}$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Z_2$-graded complex vector space, and let $\rho:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ be an even representation, meaning $\rho([X,Y]_{\mathfrak g})=\rho(X)\rho(Y)-\rho(Y)\rho(X)$ for all $X,Y\in\mathfrak g$ and each $\rho(X)$ preserves the grading of $V$. This is local Lie-algebra data; no global group, principal bundle, action functional, or quantum theory is selected here.

Choose a basis $T_a$ of $\mathfrak g$ and write $[T_b,T_c]_{\mathfrak g}=f^a{}_{bc}T_a$. A local gauge potential is a $\mathfrak g$-valued one-form $A=A_\mu^aT_a\,dx^\mu$ whose component jet generators $A_{\mu,I}^a$ are even and have ghost number zero. A matter field is a $V$-valued local field $\psi$ with each component jet generator $\psi_I^\alpha$ assigned the parity of its graded component and ghost number zero. The ghost is $c=c^aT_a$, with odd component jet generators $c_I^a$ of ghost number one. The coefficient bracket of homogeneous $\mathfrak g$-valued fields is $[X,Y]^a=f^a{}_{bc}X^bY^c$, using multiplication in the graded-commutative coefficient algebra; in particular $[c,c]^a=f^a{}_{bc}c^bc^c$ has no factor of $1/2$.

For a multi-index $I=(I_1,\ldots,I_n)\in\mathbb N^n$, let $\Phi_I$ denote the corresponding formal jet generator of a field component $\Phi$. The finite-jet local algebra $\mathcal F_U$ is $C^\infty(U)$ tensored with the polynomial algebra in its even jet generators and the exterior algebra in its odd jet generators, where each element uses only finitely many jet generators. The total derivatives $D_\mu$ act by $D_\mu f=\partial_\mu f$ on $f\in C^\infty(U)$ and $D_\mu\Phi_I=\Phi_{I+e_\mu}$ on every jet generator; the multi-index derivatives commute.

Define the degree-one BRST operator candidate $s$ on the fields by

$$sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c],\qquad sc=-\frac12[c,c],\qquad s\psi=-\rho(c)\psi.$$

On coefficient functions set $sf=0$, and on every jet generator set $s(\Phi_I)=D_I(s\Phi)$; extend $s$ to $\mathcal F_U$ by the odd left-derivation rule $s(FG)=(sF)G+(-1)^{|F|}F(sG)$ for homogeneous $F$, where $|F|$ is total parity. The minimal sector here contains only $A,\psi,c$ and their jets. Antighosts and Nakanishi–Lautrup variables are not included; adjoining such a nonminimal pair requires separate definitions and a proof before any cohomological triviality claim. The specified data are a BRST complex once $s^2=0$, which is established for these formulas in the following nilpotence lemma.

references.title: Glenn Barnich, Friedemann Brandt, and Marc Henneaux, Local BRST cohomology in gauge theories
references.locator: §§2.2–2.3 and 4.1–4.2: Yang–Mills-type gauge and ghost fields, BRST sign conventions, finite-jet local functions, and local forms.

items.title: Nilpotence of the Finite-Jet Non-Abelian BRST Differential
items.statement: Let $n\geq 1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty and open, let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra, and let $V=V_{\bar 0}\oplus V_{\bar 1}$ be a finite-dimensional graded complex vector space with an even Lie-algebra representation $\rho:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$. Form the graded-commutative finite-jet algebra over $C^\infty(U)$ from an even $\mathfrak g$-valued local one-form $A=A_\mu^aT_a\,dx^\mu$, a ghost $c=c^aT_a$ with odd components of ghost number one, and matter fields $\psi^\alpha$ of fixed component parity and ghost number zero. Let $D_\mu$ be the total derivatives on coefficient functions and formal field jets, and let $s$ be the left odd derivation of ghost number one specified by $sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$, $sc=-\tfrac12[c,c]$, $s\psi=-\rho(c)\psi$, and $s(D_I\Phi)=D_I(s\Phi)$ on every multi-index jet. Then $s^2=0$ on the entire finite-jet algebra and $sD_\mu=D_\mu s$ for each $\mu$.

references.title: Glenn Barnich, Friedemann Brandt, and Marc Henneaux, Local BRST cohomology in gauge theories
references.locator: §§2.2–2.3: the non-Abelian Yang–Mills-type BRST transformations, their ghost grading, and the square-zero differential; §4.1 for total derivatives on finite jets.

references.title: Joaquim Gomis, Jordi París, and Stuart Samuel, Antibracket, Antifields and Gauge-Theory Quantization

items.title: Local BRST Cohomology Modulo Total Derivatives
items.statement:
Let $n\geq1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty and open, let $\mathcal F_U$ be the finite-jet local algebra with nilpotent BRST derivation $s$ and commuting total derivatives $D_\mu$, and let $dx^1,\ldots,dx^n$ be anticommuting coordinate one-forms. For $g\in\mathbb Z$ and $0\leq p\leq n$, let $\mathcal A_U^{g,p}$ be the space of local horizontal $p$-forms of ghost number $g$, namely finite sums of $dx^{\mu_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{\mu_p}$ with coefficients in the ghost-number-$g$ part of $\mathcal F_U$. Define the horizontal differential $d_H:=dx^\mu D_\mu$; its square is $d_H^2a=dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu D_\mu D_\nu a=\tfrac12dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu[D_\mu,D_\nu]a=0$. Extend $s$ to horizontal forms by $s(dx^\mu\wedge a)=-dx^\mu\wedge sa$. Since $sD_\mu=D_\mu s$, one has $s(d_Ha)=-dx^\mu\wedge D_\mu(sa)=-d_H(sa)$, hence $sd_H+d_Hs=0$.

For $p=0$, set $\mathcal A_U^{g,-1}=\{0\}$. The local BRST cohomology modulo total derivatives in bidegree $(g,p)$ is

$$H^{g,p}(s\mid d_H):=\frac{\{a\in\mathcal A_U^{g,p}:\text{there is }b\in\mathcal A_U^{g+1,p-1}\text{ with }sa+d_Hb=0\}}{\{sm+d_Hn:m\in\mathcal A_U^{g-1,p},\ n\in\mathcal A_U^{g,p-1}\}}.$$

The denominator is a subspace of the numerator: for $a=sm+d_Hn$, choose $b=sn$ and compute $sa+d_Hb=s^2m+sd_Hn+d_Hsn=0$. For $p=0$, $n=b=0$ and the same verification reduces to $s^2m=0$. This is cohomology of the specified local jet algebra and horizontal differential; it is not cohomology of a physical state space or Hilbert space. Interpreting $d_H$-exact top forms as equal local functionals additionally assumes compact support or boundary conditions that make the corresponding surface term vanish.

references.title: Glenn Barnich, Friedemann Brandt, and Marc Henneaux, Local BRST cohomology in gauge theories
references.locator: §§2.3 and 4.1–4.5: local functions on finite jet spaces, local forms, the horizontal differential, and the relative cocycle/coboundary equations.

references.title: Joaquim Gomis, Jordi París, and Stuart Samuel, Antibracket, Antifields and Gauge-Theory Quantization

items.title: Classical BV Antibracket and Yang–Mills Master-Action Data
items.statement:
Use the local field data and BRST convention on an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ given by a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a graded representation space $V$, an even $\mathfrak g$-valued gauge potential $A_\mu$, an odd ghost $c$ of ghost number $1$, and matter components $\psi^\alpha$ of parity $\epsilon_\alpha$ and ghost number $0$. For every field or ghost coordinate $\Phi^A$ of parity $\epsilon_A$ and ghost number $g_A$, introduce an antifield $\Phi_A^*$ of parity $\epsilon_A+1\pmod 2$ and ghost number $-1-g_A$. Thus $A^*$ and the antifields of even matter are odd of ghost number $-1$, while $c^*$ is even of ghost number $-2$. The minimal sector consists of $A,\psi,c$ and these antifields.

For a finite-dimensional canonical coordinate algebra, take the polynomial algebra in the even coordinates tensor the exterior algebra in the odd coordinates. In the local-field notation, use finite-jet local functionals with variational derivatives only when the chosen domain makes those derivatives and integrations by parts well-defined; compact support or boundary conditions that kill surface terms are part of that domain. For homogeneous functionals $F,G$, define the canonical antibracket by

$$
(F,G):=\sum_A\left(\frac{\partial_r F}{\partial\Phi^A}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial\Phi_A^*}-\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial\Phi_A^*}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial\Phi^A}\right),
$$

with an integral over $U$ replacing the sum in a local-field expression. Left and right derivatives are the graded derivatives acting from the indicated side. Write $|F|\in\mathbb Z_2$ for the parity and $\operatorname{gh}(F)\in\mathbb Z$ for the ghost number of a homogeneous functional $F$. The bracket has parity and ghost number

$$|(F,G)|=|F|+|G|+1\pmod 2,\qquad \operatorname{gh}((F,G))=\operatorname{gh}(F)+\operatorname{gh}(G)+1.$$

For homogeneous $F,G,H$, its shifted graded-skew identity and Jacobi identity are

$$ (F,G)=-(-1)^{(|F|+1)(|G|+1)}(G,F), $$

$$ ((F,G),H)+(-1)^{(|F|+1)(|G|+|H|)}((G,H),F)+(-1)^{(|H|+1)(|F|+|G|)}((H,F),G)=0. $$

The bracket is a graded biderivation, with the exact Leibniz identities

$$ (F,GH)=(F,G)H+(-1)^{|G||H|}(F,H)G,\qquad (FG,H)=F(G,H)+(-1)^{|F||G|}G(F,H). $$

A regular finite-dimensional canonical domain has no nonzero central element of ghost number $1$: an element central against every coordinate has all coordinate derivatives zero and is a numerical constant. A formal local-functional domain used below must separately satisfy this same no-ghost-number-one-center condition.

Let a local gauge parameter be a smooth map $\lambda:U\to\mathfrak g$, and define its infinitesimal action on the fields by $\delta_\lambda A_\mu=\partial_\mu\lambda+[A_\mu,\lambda]$ and $\delta_\lambda\psi=-\rho(\lambda)\psi$. Write these variations as $\delta_\lambda\Phi^i=R^i_\alpha[\Phi]\lambda^\alpha$, where $R$ is the resulting linear differential operator in $\lambda$. Assume this declared gauge action is irreducible: if $\delta_\lambda\Phi^i\equiv0$ for every field configuration, then $\lambda\equiv0$. Assume also that its Lie-algebra action closes off shell, meaning its commutator closes without using equations of motion, and that no additional gauge symmetry is included. Let $S_0[A,\psi]$ be a specified local classical action invariant under these transformations. Write $s_0$ for the BRST operator on the minimal fields given by $s_0A_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$, $s_0c=-\tfrac12[c,c]$, and $s_0\psi=-\rho(c)\psi$. The minimal BV functional candidate is

$$S_{\mathrm{BV}}:=S_0+\int_U d^nx\,\sum_A(-1)^{\epsilon_A}\Phi_A^*\,s_0\Phi^A,$$

where each product is in the displayed order and the same left/right derivative convention is used in the antibracket. It is a **classical master action** exactly when it satisfies the classical master equation $(S_{\mathrm{BV}},S_{\mathrm{BV}})=0$; the displayed formula alone does not assert that a particular $S_0$ satisfies that equation.

The optional nonminimal sector adds an odd antighost $\bar c^a$ of ghost number $-1$, an even auxiliary field $b^a$ of ghost number $0$, and their antifields, with the BV functional term $-\bar c_a^*b^a$ giving $s\bar c=b$ and $sb=0$. This definition makes no cohomological contractibility claim for that pair. The formal local-field notation does not define an infinite-dimensional measure, a BV Laplacian $\Delta$, a path integral, or the quantum master equation.

items.title: Canonical Antibracket Generates the Declared BRST Field Variations
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal B$ be the finite-dimensional algebra that is polynomial in even canonical coordinates and exterior in odd canonical coordinates $\Phi^A,\Phi_A^*$. Give each homogeneous minimal coordinate $\Phi^A$ parity $\epsilon_A\in\{0,1\}$ and ghost number $g_A$, and give its antifield parity $\epsilon_A+1\pmod 2$ and ghost number $-1-g_A$. Use the canonical antibracket

$$ (F,G)=\sum_A\left(\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial\Phi^A}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial\Phi_A^*}-\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial\Phi_A^*}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial\Phi^A}\right). $$

Suppose each $s_0\Phi^A$ is independent of all antifields, has parity $\epsilon_A+1\pmod 2$ and ghost number $g_A+1$, and let $S_0$ be even of ghost number zero and independent of antifields. Define $S:=S_0+\sum_A(-1)^{\epsilon_A}\Phi_A^*s_0\Phi^A$, with the displayed product order. Then $(S,\Phi^A)=s_0\Phi^A$ for each minimal coordinate. For a local-field version on a nonempty open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, use fields $\Phi^A(x)$ and antifields $\Phi_A^*(x)$ with the same parity and ghost-number assignments, replace coordinate derivatives in the bracket by variational derivatives and the sum by $\int_U d^nx$, and set $S_U:=S_{0,U}+\int_U d^nx\,\sum_A(-1)^{\epsilon_A}\Phi_A^*(x)s_0\Phi^A(x)$. If this domain makes the variational derivatives and integrations by parts well-defined and its boundary term vanishes, then $(S_U,\Phi^A(x))=s_0\Phi^A(x)$ pointwise.

items.title: Classical Master Equation and Nilpotence of the BV Differential
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal B$ be the graded-commutative canonical field/antifield algebra of the preceding definition: $|\Phi^A|=\epsilon_A$, $\operatorname{gh}(\Phi^A)=g_A$, $|\Phi_A^*|=\epsilon_A+1$, and $\operatorname{gh}(\Phi_A^*)=-1-g_A$. Its canonical antibracket is odd, has ghost number $+1$, and satisfies the shifted skew and Jacobi identities stated there. Assume the center of $\mathcal B$ contains no nonzero element of ghost number one. In the finite-dimensional coordinate algebra this follows because a central element has zero derivative with respect to every field and antifield coordinate and is therefore a numerical constant; for a formal local-functional domain it is an explicit hypothesis. For any even $S_{\mathrm{BV}}\in\mathcal B$ of ghost number zero, define $sF:=(S_{\mathrm{BV}},F)$. Then $s^2=0$ on $\mathcal B$ if and only if the classical master equation $(S_{\mathrm{BV}},S_{\mathrm{BV}})=0$ holds.

In the local-field case of the preceding definition, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty and open, let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra, and let $\rho$ be the stated parity-preserving representation on the graded matter space. Take the minimal fields $A,\psi,c$ and their antifields, with $\delta_\lambda A_\mu=\partial_\mu\lambda+[A_\mu,\lambda]$ and $\delta_\lambda\psi=-\rho(\lambda)\psi$ for every admitted smooth $\lambda:U\to\mathfrak g$. Assume $[\delta_\lambda,\delta_\mu]=\delta_{[\lambda,\mu]}$ without equations of motion, where $[\lambda,\mu](x):=[\lambda(x),\mu(x)]_{\mathfrak g}$, and that $\delta_\lambda\Phi\equiv0$ for every field configuration implies $\lambda\equiv0$. Let $S_0[A,\psi]$ be a local functional with well-defined variational derivatives, invariant under these transformations. Choose a functional domain and support or boundary conditions for which the antibracket, integrations by parts, and gauge-variation identity are well-defined and boundary terms vanish. For $s_0A_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$, $s_0c=-\tfrac12[c,c]$, and $s_0\psi=-\rho(c)\psi$, form the minimal action $S_{\mathrm{BV}}=S_0+\int_U d^nx\,\sum_A(-1)^{\epsilon_A}\Phi_A^*s_0\Phi^A$ in the order specified in the definition. Then this minimal action satisfies the classical master equation $(S_{\mathrm{BV}},S_{\mathrm{BV}})=0$.

title: Non-Abelian BRST Cohomology and Classical BV Data — Examples

items.title: Component Check of the SU(2) BRST Differential
items.statement:
Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{su}(2)$ with basis $T_a=-\tfrac{i}{2}\sigma_a$, where

$$
\sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Then $[T_a,T_b]=\epsilon_{ab}{}^cT_c$. Use the defining representation on $V=\mathbb C^2$, so $\rho(T_a)=T_a$, and let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty open set, where $n$ is a nonnegative integer. Place $V$ wholly in either even or odd parity. For $n\geq1$, use the finite-jet algebra of the earlier BRST definition. For $n=0$, $U=\mathbb R^0$ is a point: take the graded-commutative algebra over $\mathbb C$ freely generated by the two matter components of the chosen parity and three odd ghosts, with no gauge-potential components or positive-order jets. On these algebras, with even gauge potential $A_\mu=A_\mu^aT_a$, odd ghosts $c^a$, and homogeneous matter components $\psi^\alpha$, define the odd left derivation $s$ by $sf=0$ on coefficient functions, by prolongation $s(D_I\Phi)=D_I(s\Phi)$ on jets, and by

$$sA_\mu^a=\partial_\mu c^a+\epsilon^a{}_{bc}A_\mu^bc^c,\qquad sc^a=-\frac12\epsilon^a{}_{bc}c^bc^c,\qquad s\psi=-c^aT_a\psi.$$

The operator $s$ squares to zero on these generators and their formal spacetime jets.

items.title: The SU(2) Ghost Sector Solves the Classical Master Equation
items.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ have basis $T_a$ with $[T_b,T_c]=\epsilon^a{}_{bc}T_a$. Form the finite graded-commutative coordinate algebra $\mathcal B=\mathbb C[c_1^*,c_2^*,c_3^*]\otimes\Lambda(c^1,c^2,c^3)$, where each $c^a$ is odd of ghost number $1$ and each $c_a^*$ is even of ghost number $-2$. Use the canonical antibracket

$$
(F,G)=\sum_{a=1}^3\left(\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial c^a}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial c_a^*}-\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial c_a^*}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial c^a}\right).
$$

For $S_{\mathrm{CE}}=\tfrac12c_a^*\epsilon^a{}_{bc}c^bc^c$, the element $S_{\mathrm{CE}}$ is even with ghost number zero and satisfies $(S_{\mathrm{CE}},S_{\mathrm{CE}})=0$. Hence the Hamiltonian differential $sF=(S_{\mathrm{CE}},F)$ is nilpotent. This is only the finite-dimensional non-Abelian ghost sector; it is not a Yang–Mills action or a quantum field theory.
